verdict.rationale: Probes show irs.gov serves a content robots.txt that agents can consult (for example, /dmaf is not disallowed). However, the application host running the EIN online assistant returned HTTP 503 for robots.txt and has no stable published file, so an agent cannot learn the rules for the transactional surface before fetching. missing for 10: a stable robots.txt on the app host (sa.www4.irs.gov), direct retrieval evidence of the irs.gov robots.txt contents, and any agent-specific guidance for the transactional flows.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service publishes a real robots.txt, so an agent can know what it may read before fetching anything

citations.quote: /dmaf is not disallowed by irs.gov robots.txt
the EIN online assistant runs on an application host with no stable published robots.txt; the irs.gov content robots.txt does not govern it.
